chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah, who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who owns a pasture (dhiyah) and its boundaries extend to twenty miles, or less, or more. A man comes to him and says, 'Give me from the grazing of your pasture, and I will give you such and such a dirham.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If the pasture belongs to him, there is no harm.'

key_terms.اَلرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell grazing rights for private land in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of leasing private pastureland (*dhiyah*) for grazing, establishing that ownership grants the right to monetize its utility through agreed-upon compensation. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that private property rights extend to the benefits derived from the land, provided there is no explicit prohibition, thereby validating commercial transactions involving natural resources under Islamic law.
